what: foot line per monster frame. footRow = last row (0-based, from top) with any opaque pixel; gapBelow = empty rows under it. A billboard anchored at its bottom edge stands on the floor when gapBelow is 0.
howToUse: world y of the quad bottom = floorY - gapBelow * (quadHeight / imageHeight). Or simply ignore: the worst case is 1 px, which is under 2% of the sprite height.

distanceFrames.what: v2 monster frames in art/dungeon/monsters_v2/<monster>_<anim>_<n>_<set>.png (static: <monster>_<set>.png = idle_1). The old fixed 80x60/50x40/30x25 frames in art/dungeon/ are kept unchanged.

setBySquares.0: close (own square; not used for monsters)

distanceFrames.rule: Pick the set by squares ahead (Chebyshev distance for side squares). Quad height in world units = size.worldHeight (levels/monsters.json) x wall height (CELL_SIZE 2.0); quad width = quad height x imageW/imageH of THAT set (aspect differs per monster and set, never 80/60). Bottom-centre anchor on the floor (gapBelow is 0 for every v2 frame). NearestFilter, no mipmaps. Swap the texture AND the quad aspect when the set changes, and change it on the step, so each set draws at ~1 texel per screen pixel at its own distance.
distanceFrames.nativeHeight: imageH = round(worldHeight x wallPx[squares]); wallPx = on-screen height of a full wall at the centre of that square = 2.0 x f / z, f = (viewH/2)/tan(fov/2), z = view depth of the square centre with the eye at the back edge of the party square. Canvas = union of all 12 frames, so the tallest pose touches row 0 and idle is a little shorter.
distanceFrames.rerun: When camera.json lands: python3 build_monsters_v2.py --camera <path> && python3 build_monster_anchor.py && python3 ../preview/build_monsters_v2_preview.py
